A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same work. Their algorithms, theorems, and complete appendices can be matched despite reformatting, renumbering, and relocation of the proof overview.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees, proofs, and analytical examples. Neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper. Its revised counterexample and LQR derivation are mathematical arguments, with no experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains D-optimal initialization, constrained value/reward regression, null-space value perturbations, and greedy interaction. The optimization procedures in Algorithms 2–5 are also retained.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or benchmarks for training or evaluation. The revised MDP and LQR examples concern theoretical coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Added references to randomization methods expand related work only.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing protocols.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical supplementary analyses. Changes to mathematical counterexamples are assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical concentration arguments are retained.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries or findings are added, removed, or revised. The principal regret and sample-complexity bounds in Section 5 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The supporting LQR argument changes substantially: v1 Appendix D claims closure for arbitrary quadratic-feature parameters, whereas v2 Appendix E restricts it to positive-semidefinite quadratic forms and supplies a new Schur-complement derivation with general Gaussian covariance. Section 3.1 also replaces the two-state deterministic counterexample with a three-state probabilistic construction. The principal regret theorems and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same algorithmic contribution and headline regret guarantee for deterministic dynamics, large action spaces, stochastic rewards, and stochastic initial states.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies LQR coverage to a convex subclass, adds discussion of difficulties with feature normalization in Section 3.1, and explains in Appendix C.2 why avoiding trajectory expectations enables the deterministic span argument. These refine applicability and mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: The oracle pseudocode, parameter specifications, and computational complexity statements are retained. No code/data access information or experimental implementation details are introduced.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ishfaq et al. (2021, 2023) and discusses their randomization assumptions and Langevin Monte Carlo approach. Sections 3.1–3.2 refine criticism of prior norm assumptions. Wu and Sun's updated publication citation refers to the same existing work.

P1.justification: The proof overview moves from v1 Section 6 to v2 Appendix B, and the low-inherent-error discussion becomes Section 5.3. Introduction and related-work prose receive localized edits, while the LQR explanation is rewritten; most remaining exposition is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different conference layout throughout, including title and author formatting, repeated headers, typography, spacing, and algorithm placement. Table 1's caption moves above the table, and the contents listing expands to include the main sections. No empirical figures or tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through narrower LQR coverage, expanded related work, and the deterministic-decomposition explanation. However, its replacement Example 1 states that the feature norm is p instead of sqrt(p), and the revised LQR proof uses P_uu inverse under positive semidefiniteness without addressing singularity. These unresolved mathematical issues make the net benefit uncertain, while the principal algorithm and guarantees remain unchanged.
